content:
Rumors suggest that the AirPods 5 will make their debut next week alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, as well as the iPhone Ultra. Here is what we currently know about the new AirPods.

The AirPods 5 is expected to launch at the September 9 event, available in two models, but will not feature a camera.

Apple's biggest annual event will be held next week on September 9. In addition to a series of new iPhone and Apple Watch models, as well as potentially some home products, the AirPods 5 is also expected to launch at the same time.

The AirPods 4 debuted in 2024, and Apple's AirPods have historically followed an update cycle of two to three years. The original AirPods launched in 2016, AirPods 2 in 2019, AirPods 3 in 2021, and AirPods 4 in 2024. According to this timeline, a new product launch this year broadly aligns with the established pattern.

However, somewhat surprisingly, rumors and leaks about the new AirPods have not been particularly numerous so far.

In recent months, most of the rumors surrounding the AirPods have centered on a new model equipped with a camera. Earlier, a video leaked from inside Apple showed a model with a camera, leading to speculation that it was about to launch.

However, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has stated that the AirPods with a camera won't arrive until 2027. But he expects the camera-less AirPods 5 to debut at the September event. In an earlier article, he wrote:

In a separate X post, Gurman added that the AirPods 5 will be available in two different models:

  • Equipped with Active Noise Cancellation (ANC)
  • Without ANC

In an earlier report, Gurman mentioned that he expects the AirPods 5 will not feature the heart rate sensor found on the AirPods Pro 3, but Apple is "researching adding more health features to the AirPods in the future, including a body temperature sensor." He also mentioned that Apple is developing an "H3 chip designed to reduce latency and improve sound quality."

Whether the AirPods 5 will adopt the H3 chip remains unknown. When Apple initially introduced the H2 chip, it was exclusive to the AirPods Pro lineup.

However, new health sensors could potentially be added to the AirPods 5, and the H3 chip is also a possibility. Beyond that, details about the AirPods 5 remain fairly limited so far. Alternatively, just as with the AirPods Max 2 launched earlier this year, Apple may still surprise us when it unveils the AirPods 5.

What features would you like to see on the next-generation AirPods from Apple? Let us know in the comments section.
